title: Sandboxing and resource limits
outcome: Explain sandboxing and resource limits using the deciding step in this fictional service.
scenario: Bound a student program. A toy sandbox forbids network access, allows at most two seconds and limits output to 20 MB.
given: A uses one second and writes 2 MB. B tries to contact a website. These are declared trial records.

steps.label: Check A
steps.detail: One second and 2 MB fit both resource limits.

steps.label: Deny B network call
steps.detail: Stop the prohibited network action regardless of its purpose.

explanation: Sandbox controls bound reach and resource use. Passing an output limit cannot cancel a network or time restriction.

counterfactual.change: A takes three seconds but still writes 2 MB.
counterfactual.prediction: Stop A for exceeding the time allowance.
counterfactual.reason: The independent two-second limit remains binding.

student_task: Check A against both resource limits and B against network isolation. Why must A stop after three seconds even if its output remains only 2 MB?
teacher_answer: Neither program receives network permission. One second and 2 MB fit both resource limits. Stop the prohibited network action regardless of its purpose. Changed case: Stop A for exceeding the time allowance. The independent two-second limit remains binding.
project_evidence: For the Grounded Learning Service, retain an annotated trace and the changed-case result. Name the contract or evidence that makes the deciding step valid, so another team can review it.
limits: These controls are not a complete security proof; implementation and escape risks still require review.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice, distinct from the reserved independent case. These stipulated records illustrate reasoning; no real service execution or learner outcome is claimed.
